scope: Fail-closed pixel-lineage audit for true wrist-only DROID to Cosmos3 third-person SFT data
summary: The local audit implementation now verifies every derived condition and sampled future against hash-bound, explicitly named DROID camera crops before the wrist-only dataset can be accepted.
evidence: All 60 Cosmos3-focused CPU tests pass in 0.66 seconds, including two new audit gate tests.
Targeted Ruff, py_compile, and git diff whitespace checks pass.
The audit verifies source, target, and condition SHA-256 values and checks all 348 planned train/validation records rather than sampling records.
The frozen gates require at least 0.97 SSIM for wrist condition lineage, derived frame-0 wrist lineage, and sampled named-exterior future lineage, plus a 0.05 wrist-over-exterior condition margin.
The audit records the canonical DROID composite, resized wrist, resized named-exterior, and 768x432 RGB comparison coordinate frames without mixing them implicitly.
lessons: Declaring a wrist-only transform in metadata is insufficient; decoded pixels must be checked against the hash-bound source cameras before training promotion.
A real third-person target is valid supervision and withheld evaluation evidence, but must never be mislabeled or passed as the inference condition.
limitations: WORKING applies only to the local audit implementation and tests; the remote materialized dataset has not yet been audited because SSH access is blocked by the current sandbox.
No Cosmos3 wrist-only training, generated video, strict quality acceptance, or public demo is claimed.
next_actions: When remote access is available, sync the audit, run it in a new immutable directory over the completed 344-train/4-validation dataset, and ledger the measured result.
Allow the gated DCP conversion and two-A800 backpropagation smoke to proceed only after checkpoint and dataset verification; keep formal 500-step SFT pending eight free GPUs.
